title: LSASS memory accessed with full-access masks and an unbacked remote thread injected by PowerShell on scranton
summary: On 2020-05-02 03:05:16 UTC on scranton.dmevals.local, C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe (PID 2976, user DMEVALS\pbeesly) opened C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe (PID 736) with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff (Sysmon EID 10) and created a remote thread in it (Sysmon EID 8, NewThreadId 912) starting at 0x00000117610E0000 with StartModule '-' (code in unbacked memory). Security EID 4656 independently shows the same PowerShell process (SubjectUserName pbeesly) requesting handles to \Device\HarddiskVolume2\Windows\System32\lsass.exe with AccessMask 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff at 23:05:16 local (=03:05:16Z). That PowerShell process was launched at 02:58:44 by C:\Windows\System32\control.exe with a hidden command line that decodes an ASCII payload from C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\monkey.png (steganography) and IEXes it, and it then compiled C# in memory via csc.exe (Temp\RES2758.tmp) and wrote a .pfx to Downloads. A second in-memory loader (reflective delegate via UnsafeNativeMethods.GetProcAddress plus a base64 shellcode blob) was logged for the same host/user at 03:21:29 after the 03:18:30 restart initiated by pbeesly. This is LSASS memory access/credential dumping (T1003.001) on scranton by the pbeesly session; the same account then used PsExec64 with the cleartext password of dmevals\pbeesly against \\NASHUA (PSEXESVC installed 4x on nashua, python.exe run from C:\Windows\Temp).

title: wsmprovhost.exe full-access handle to LSASS on nashua is Get-Process -IncludeUserName enumeration (benign)
summary: On 2020-05-02 03:09:29 UTC on nashua.dmevals.local, C:\windows\system32\wsmprovhost.exe (PID 7720, pbeesly PS-remoting session) accessed C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff. The same 0x1f3fff mask was requested against a long list of unrelated processes (ApplicationFrameHost.exe, browser_broker.exe, conhost.exe, ctfmon.exe, DllHost.exe, dwm.exe, Explorer.EXE, fontdrvhost.exe, LogonUI.exe), and the PS remoting script block recorded at 03:09:28 on nashua is 'Get-Process -IncludeUserName | Select-Object UserName,SessionId | ...' - the standard signature of Get-Process -IncludeUserName enumerating process owners, not targeted LSASS reading. No dump write or remote thread into lsass exists for this host (Sysmon EID 8 query for nashua returned nothing).

evidence.value: Get-Process -IncludeUserName | Select-Object UserName,SessionId | Where-Object { $_.UserName -like "*\$env:USERNAME" } | Sort-Object SessionId -Unique

title: Only lsass.exe itself wrote to the SAM hive; no SAM dump or hive copy observed
summary: Registry-write telemetry matching *SAM* on 2020-05-02 contains only two events, both on scranton.dmevals.local: lsass.exe setting HKLM\SAM\SAM\Domains\Account\F at 03:19:10 (immediately after the 03:18:30 restart initiated by pbeesly) and LogonUI.exe setting the LogonUI\SessionData\2\LoggedOnSAMUser value at 03:20:46 - i.e. legitimate post-logon SAM bookkeeping by the SAM owner process. No hive extraction tooling was observed: Security 4688 has no reg.exe/reg save, esentutl, ntdsutil or vssadmin executions, and no file-create event writes the SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM hive files. SAM-hash theft is therefore not demonstrated in this window (LSASS itself was attacked instead - see the T1003.001 finding).

evidence.value: The process C:\Windows\System32\RuntimeBroker.exe (SCRANTON) has initiated the restart of computer SCRANTON on behalf of user DMEVALS\pbeesly for the following reason: Other (Unplanned)

title: Kerberos ticketing is AES256-only service/TGT traffic - no RC4 Kerberoasting pattern
summary: In windows.security the 28 Kerberos service-ticket requests (EID 4769) are all TicketEncryptionType 0x12 (AES256) for user pbeesly@DMEVALS.LOCAL against machine accounts (ServiceName NEWYORK$, NASHUA$, krbtgt) with Status 0x0, and the 14 TGT requests (EID 4768) are likewise 0x12 for pbeesly/krbtgt - no RC4 (0x17/0x18) ticket storm and no anomalous service SPNs, so Kerberoasting is not evidenced. In the separate, non-overlapping zeek capture window (2020-04-30) every Kerberos record carries cipher aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96 and the only failures are AS-REQ exchanges answered with KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED for pbeesly (normal pre-authentication, which also argues against AS-REP roasting of that account).
